restrictions: Target sha256-r38-prefix-v1 exactly: SHA-256 steps 0..37 on every padded block, the standard IV once, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all eight digest words; outputs two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1, M0 || M1' with equal digests.

Construction: the memory-efficient A0-variant attack (design of 2d1c4fc2 and fb176310 on ePrint 2026/1120 / 2026/1080; per-class row-16 programs as in 08be594), our implementation experiments/a0p38.py, with our characteristic P8 and the accepted event rows 16..22 (row 19 on signed differences) plus a direct output comparison.

Cost: exact ledger ledger_a0p.py: N_FB = 1,510,856,422,634,357,630,235,398 first blocks, 32 classes of 24,576 variants (786,432 in all), per-class row-16 programs of 1,438 to 1,482 instructions (mean 1462.25) per 256 variants, executed counts; T x 2728 = 466886209777192599903152252449; claimed 87.14536.
Success probability at least 0.39 under H1, H2 (q3_model 2^-97.0000), H3, by Bonferroni per first block, independent first blocks and Chebyshev caps.
Memory 2^28.10 bytes (online 3,659,904 bytes; the preprocessing peak).

heuristics.statement: For M0 uniform on {0,1}^512 (two fresh random words per first block), CV1 = F_38(IV, M0) behaves as a uniform 256-bit value for the events of one fixed variant (W7, W16..W22 and E16x distributed as in Lemma 5.1).
heuristics.scope: g, the per-first-block success probability and the expected work.
heuristics.extrapolation: The premise of the A0-variant lineage; the organizer experiment a0p-online-r38 runs the program on real first blocks.
heuristics.limitations: A premise about the first-block compression.

heuristics.statement: The average over the 786,432 selected variants (32 classes) of Pr[the pair is in the accepted event (rows 16..22 with row 19 on signed differences, equal outputs) | good pair] is at least q3_model = 2^-97.0000.
heuristics.scope: N_FB and the whole attack term.
heuristics.extrapolation: 20 multilevel-splitting runs (seeds 4001..4020) with the variants of the selected classes: mean 2^-96.2971, one-sided 99% Student bound 2^-96.9988, bootstrap 2^-96.8745, 84,957 verified collisions (two stalled runs counted as 0); an independent Python implementation (the organizer replica, a lower-bound event restricted to four row-19 patterns and 512 sampled variants): 480 development replicates, mean 2^-96.2059; organizer replica a0p-q3-r38 with a frozen pass rule.
heuristics.limitations: Participant-run Monte Carlo with a heavy-tailed middle stage; the replica tests a reduced version.

heuristics.statement: The average over successes of the expected number of other row-16 passes of the same first block is at most 2^-5.1.
heuristics.scope: The Bonferroni factor of a first block.
heuristics.extrapolation: 750 rebuilt successes: 6 other row-16 passes among 153,649,152 evaluated variants of the passing classes; 99% Poisson limit 2^-5.69.

heuristics.statement: The computation spent on the characteristic search, S and the class data, and all development is at most A_C + A_S + DEV = 2^48 + 2^50 + 2^50 target compressions.
heuristics.extrapolation: One 10-core machine, less than 2^22 core-seconds in all; holds at up to 2^27 compressions per core-second.
heuristics.limitations: Wall-clock bound; with A_C = 2^84 the ledger gives time_log2 = 87.29984 (+0.15448).

heuristics.statement: One instruction on a 256-bit plane costs one word operation (the 256-bit word RAM of the cost model); each class's row-16 program is charged at its executed instruction count, loads and stores included (expected work at the mean over the classes, the work cap at the maximum).
heuristics.extrapolation: Executed instruction by instruction and compared with the scalar definition on sampled batches (selftest, a0p-online-r38).
